who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent in Claude Code, dst-1113; the cause read out of the code by a Claude Opus 5.5 lane
where: crates/blaze-lints: `blaze/test_code.rs` (`is_test_code`, `is_test_def`), `blaze/env_read.rs`, `blaze/goose_fields.rs`; seen with `blaze check -p blaze-sim --all-targets` on blaze-vm, blaze built from dd5e84a0ae, e1f6f24432 and 78c4ba8c7e
what: An `#[expect(blaze::<lint>, reason = "..")]` on production code silences the finding and is then reported `warning: this lint expectation is unfulfilled`, for `blaze::write_only_field`, `constant_argument`, `parallel_collections`, `env_read` and `untyped_index`. Three runs on crates/blaze-sim: expectation present, no finding and an unfulfilled warning; expectation deleted, the finding is back. So the crate cannot reach zero findings for these lints by an expectation.
cost: two extra rounds on blaze-sim (I deleted expectations that were doing their job), and four warnings left in a crate that is otherwise clean
cause: `--all-targets` lints a library twice, plain and built with `--test`. In the test build the crate's `target_kind` is `Test` (its `manifest_kind` stays `Lib`), and lints that ask `target_kind` whether code is test code take the whole library for test code and judge nothing in it; the engine still records every `#[expect]` there and reports it unfulfilled. `untyped_index` differs: its facts fold every body of the crate (`goose_fields`), test bodies included in the test build, so its verdict on a production field differs between the two builds (read from the code, the changed fact not identified).
whys: what code is (production or test) was answered from how the crate is being built; each lint asked for itself (27 files through `is_test_code`, four more directly); nothing states that a production item's verdict must be the same in both builds, so no test compares them; findings repeated across the two builds print once, which hid that most lints already ran twice and these did not
class: an expectation judged in a build where its lint judges the code differently than in the build that fulfils it
prevention: fulfilment belongs to the attribute, not to one build: an `#[expect]` is fulfilled when its lint fires under it in at least one build of the manifest target linted in the run, and reported unfulfilled only when every such build that holds it says so; decided where a package's units come together and repeated findings are already printed once. Being built on branch lints-both-builds-1114. Tried first and taken back (commit f58ee2f228): asking the manifest target what code is, so the lints judge production code in the test build too. Its four tests passed, but a blaze built from it gave `failed errors=16` on crates/blaze-sim (twelve `used only by tests` on public draws, test calls counted by `constant_argument`) where main's blaze exits 0: it changes what lints report, which this bug does not need. Whether a production item's verdict should be equal in both builds is a separate question for the lints' owner; for `only_used_in_tests` it cannot be, since only the test build sees the tests' uses.
workaround: none in user code; blaze-sim keeps the true expectations and carries the unfulfilled warnings until the engine fix lands
